---
title: "How do I assess a monotonic relationship using ranked observations?"
---

## Question

How do I assess a monotonic relationship using ranked observations?

## Decide which method fits

Identify two aligned numeric or ordinal variables; plot the paired data; use Spearman's rank correlation when a monotonic relationship is the target.

## Worked example: faithful

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("faithful")
fit <- ru_apply("spearman_correlation", d, x="eruptions", y="waiting")
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$estimate))
```

Spearman's coefficient describes how eruption length and waiting time vary together in rank order. A large coefficient does not imply that every association is linear or causal.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("spearman_correlation", your_data, x="first_numeric_column", y="second_numeric_column")
```

Spearman's rho does not capture every nonlinear shape. For a strong U-shaped pattern, use a plot rather than relying on one number.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("spearman_correlation")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
